name: seat_second_cursor_click
description: SECOND POINTER SEAT (9b-ii / 9b-ii-c): two focusable rows. The primary cursor (seat 0) rests on r1; a second seat (seat 7, an X11 MPX master pointer or a Wayland wl_seat) presses on r3. Before the seat model every pointer wrote the ONE mouse state, so the second cursor's press landed at the first cursor's position; and before 9b-ii-c the runner's click-to-focus scan read the PRIMARY's hit test for every press, so seat 7's click would have focused r1. Asserts: seat 7's press focuses r3 while the primary still hovers r1; the primary's own click afterwards focuses r1 - the two cursors keep separate positions; and a seat-7 press+release on r3 again re-focuses r3 after the primary click, i.e. the seat's state persisted across the primary's activity.
